title: Prince of Ning rebellion
text: The Prince of Ning rebellion was a revolt during the Ming dynasty in China led by Zhu Chenhao, Prince of Ning, against the reigning Zhengde Emperor. It took place in northern Jiangxi and southwestern Nanzhili and lasted from 10 July to 20 August 1519. The rebellion was ultimately quelled when the government army, led by Wang Yangming, the grand coordinator of southern Jiangxi, captured the Prince of Ning. The Prince of Ning revolt was one of two princely rebellions during the Zhengde Emperor's reign; it was preceded by the Prince of Anhua rebellion in 1510.
